dedupe_keys.name: grey and green flood protection in the upper vistula basin at sandomierz poland

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes flood protection around Sandomierz on the Upper Vistula, Poland, where precipitation and runoff are 15% and 50% above the national average and floods in 2010 and 2011 hit local communities. Designed from 2011 within the Vistula river basin management plans under the EU Water Framework and Floods Directives and finalised in 2015, the hybrid approach combines expansion, reconstruction and modernisation of embankments and pumping with renaturalisation of reservoirs and wetland restoration, plus institutional measures, to raise retention capacity and cut flood risk. The total cost was about 217 million euro, including land purchases, funded by the World Bank, with implementation expected by 2019. The page is free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal, drawing on EEA Report 14/2017 on green infrastructure and flood management. Caveats: avoided damages are estimates, green and grey benefits are not separated, and completion was still pending when the page was written. It illustrates investment in combined grey and green flood defences in a large river basin; a related record is the Physical Vulnerability Database for critical infrastructure.
name: Grey and green flood protection in the Upper Vistula basin at Sandomierz (Poland)
outcomes: A 217 million euro hybrid programme of embankments and green retention measures, funded by the World Bank, was planned for completion by 2019 to raise retention and reduce flood risk around Sandomierz.
